neighbours.label: ' of' standing free instead of completing the word before it: it opens its own set phrase after a comma, a verb or 'is/was' (', of course', ', of late', 'of necessity', 'of her own accord', 'came of age', 'are of no concern'), or starts a sentence or title ('Of all the...', 'Of Mice and Men'). Quiet when the word before asks for the 'of': noun of noun ('cup of coffee', 'a man of courage'), 'afraid of', 'think of', 'consists of', 'out of', 'kind of', 'because of'; partitive 'one of / all of the' stays weak.
neighbours.short: free-standing 'of' opening its own phrase (of course, of late, came of age)
fire: She will be there on time, of course, because she always is.
Of all the places to lose my keys, it had to be the beach.
He has been rather quiet, of late, and nobody knows why.
The cat left the room of her own accord.
My grandfather came of age during the long drought.
Your old debts are of no concern to the new owners.
We sold the farm of necessity, not by choice.
Of Mice and Men is on the reading list this term.
quiet: A glass of water stood beside the bed.
The roof of the barn collapsed in the storm.
She will be there on time, naturally, because she always is.
She ordered a cup of coffee and sat by the window.
He has been rather quiet recently, and nobody knows why.
The cat was afraid of the vacuum and left the room.
My grandfather grew up during the long drought.
Your old debts no longer concern the new owners.

predictions: Blind test from the label (author: blind:claude-opus-5-5, label-only). Expect most fire items to clear 0.20; risk on 'room of her own accord' and 'farm of necessity', where the free 'of' follows a noun.
